record_type_quote: In this preregistered study using experimenter-rated adherence to response instructions, we aimed to conceptually replicate and extend key findings from the latter two strands using the same dataset.

targets.authors: Baird, B. M., Lucas, R. E., & Donnellan, M. B.
targets.title: The role of response styles in the assessment of intraindividual personality variability.
targets.study_numbers_original_note: Introduction discusses relevant correlations in Study 1; replication aim is stated at paper level.
targets.evidence_quote: For this, we aimed to conceptually replicate Baird et al.’s (2017) findings that corrected response variability is correlated across different measures.
targets.outcome_quote: The present findings highlight that response variability should not be interpreted uniformly, but rather that individual differences in response variability were stable across repeated assessments, generalized across measures and even remained substantially consistent between truthful vs. careless experimental conditions. This strongly supports the conclusions by Baird et al. (2017) and Nestler et al. (2021) that response variability contains stable respondentspecific information.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Overall substantive verdict explicitly strongly supports the original conclusion. The strict reconstruction gives weaker correlations and incomplete significance but is still positive; authors attribute smaller effects to reduced reliability, rather than concluding the central finding fails.

targets.authors: Goldammer, P., Annen, H., Stöckli, P. L., & Klaus, J.
targets.title: Careless responding in questionnaire measures: Detection, impact, and remedies.
targets.evidence_quote: However, indicators targeting restricted or repetitive responding, such as longstring (Johnson, 2005), do not necessarily distinguish careful responders from careless responders equally well (Goldammer et al., 2020). A central challenge in evaluating such indicators is establishing a valid criterion for whether participants actually responded carelessly. In the present study, we addressed this problem by experimentally instructing participants to respond either truthfully or carelessly and separately monitoring their adherence to these instructions in real time.
targets.outcome_quote: Longstring showed comparatively weak discrimination in the present study, particularly for overtly careless responding. This finding is consistent with Goldammer et al. (2020), who likewise reported weak performance of longstring under experimentally induced carelessness.
targets.outcome_reasoning: New experimentally induced careless responses test the published indicator discrimination finding, explicitly agreeing on weak longstring performance. General preregistered predictions about all indicators are not imported as contradictions of this specific original finding.

reasoning: Primary target Baird is named explicitly; the second strand re-tests Goldammer’s experimental careless-response detection finding and explicitly compares longstring results. Nestler is an antecedent corroborating the Baird finding, not the named design target; other response-style and trait references motivate the study. Completed preregistered study, not a protocol. Target identification for Goldammer is less explicit than for Baird.
